accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow Baldick's Oxford Dictionary of Literary Terms and the AQA GCSE terminology guidance: caesura is a pause within a line, enjambment is a sentence running over a line break, an end-stopped line closes at the break, sibilance repeats sibilant sounds (s, sh, z) and is judged by ear, a motif recurs across a work, a semantic field is a set of words related in meaning, juxtaposition places contrasting elements side by side, and foreshadowing hints at later events. In the lab poem the marked points are checked: point 1 and point 4 are full stops inside a line, line 1 ends unpunctuated and runs on, and line 2 ends on a full stop. All passages are original.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips GCSE examiner reports name: feature-spotting without effect and vague effects ('more interesting'; build step and challenge 'label'/'vague', m3), a broad label instead of the precise term ('imagery'; build step, m4), reading a metaphorical semantic field literally ('shows there is a real war'), calling any repeated consonant sibilance and judging it by spelling (prediction 3, 'Big bold bells', 'Sure, she…', m5), swapping caesura and enjambment (prediction 2, tag feedback, challenge enj/cae), and confusing motif with foreshadowing (prediction 4).

lab_distinct.evidence: Every mechanic is a reading move on real text: tapping a semantic field inside a passage that reflows on any screen, dragging tags onto measured points in a quatrain with per-pair feedback (caesura vs end-stopped, enjambment vs end-stopped), sorting lines by sibilant sound, naming structural methods against highlighted scenes on a five-scene timeline, and assembling method + evidence + effect with vague and literal options rejected. Shingle gate passed against every flagship lab, including flag_auth and flag_craft.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find the field themselves (literal kitchen words are rejected with the reason), discover the caesura/enjambment line by tagging points and reading the feedback, learn sibilance by sound through the 'Sure, she wished' line, see each structural method light up the scenes it spans (one scene for juxtaposition, two for foreshadowing, three for a motif), and end by writing a full analytical sentence. Done messages then state each distinction.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'one striking word' for a semantic field, 'enjambment' for a mid-line full stop, 'Yes, a sound repeats' for plosive b alliteration, 'foreshadowing' for a recurring scarf, and 'naming five techniques' for exam credit; each is disproved by the step that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve tagged messages: caesura vs enjambment both ways, caesura vs sibilance, enjambment vs juxtaposition, semantic field vs motif and vs foreshadowing, foreshadowing vs juxtaposition and vs motif, label-only analysis, vague effect, semantic field vs juxtaposition, and enjambment vs juxtaposition.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text stays within the 6.5 grade limit, grouping the terms by what they act on (words, lines, whole text) with one concrete example each; adult text stays within 9.5 and gives the exam-board framing. Canvas text is a short extract, a four-line poem and one-line clues; every tag, sort and choice is repeated as a button.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate against every lesson, including Author's word choices and Writing Craft Vocabulary. Kid paragraphs each cover one family of terms; adult paragraphs give assessment context, precise distinctions, the documented mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone and 360 px Android screenshots of every step in light and dark: the passage reflows into tappable word pills, the quatrain fits with numbered points and three tag chips below, the line card sits above two sort boxes, the five scene cards fit in one row under the two-line clue, and the three analysis slots sit above full-width options that compress long text to fit.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button route (one button per passage word, 'Point n: tag' buttons, Sibilance / Not sibilance, term buttons, slot option buttons) and the canvas aria-label states the result of each move.

sources: Baldick, C. (2015), The Oxford Dictionary of Literary Terms, 4th edn (caesura, enjambment, end-stopped, sibilance, motif, juxtaposition, foreshadowing, semantic field)
AQA (2015), GCSE English Literature 8702 specification and mark scheme guidance: AO2 analyse language, form and structure, using relevant subject terminology where appropriate
AQA GCSE English Literature examiner reports (2019, 2023): feature-spotting and unsupported terminology credited little; effects must be explained
